sources.title: Naturalis — Palaemon serratus diagnosis
sources.scope: Selected actual institutional diagnosis read for upcurved normally bifid rostrum, distal gap in dorsal dentition, two posterior dorsal teeth behind orbit, triramous antennules and pigment layout. Counts vary between taxonomic sources and are not a universal model-identification measurement.

sources.title: FAO Mediterranean identification guide — Palaemon serratus
sources.scope: Actual selected PDFpage12 printed239 diagnosis and whole-body, rostrum, P2-chela and antennular drawings viewed. Also selected family characters: two anterior chelate pairs and second pleuron overlapping first/third. Reported tooth-count ranges differ from Naturalis; selected tooth cues and proportions remain unmeasured. Historical fishery/range text is not current quantitative data.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected actual PDF text and rendered figures

findings.shape: Original laterally compressed carapace and continuous tapered six-somite abdomen replace the untextured repeated rounded segments. The selected upward-curved rostrum has posterior tooth cues, a distal dorsal gap and bifid-tip cue; second pleural plates overlap the adjacent regions. Two anterior small chelate pairs, with P2 larger than P1, precede three posterior main support pairs. Separate scaphocerites, three antennular flagellar cues, five simple pleopod pairs and a narrow telson with four uropodal lobes are retained.
findings.surface: Original subdued grey-green cuticle, oblique cephalic and vertical abdominal brown bands and limited semitransparency. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue-optics calibration. The continuous cuticle deforms over the existing articulated joints; it does not exchange models between actions.
findings.movement: A short authored support/recovery bout holds planted toes and fixed segment lengths, then settles. Small anterior-claw and antenna gestures, simple pleopod strokes, mild local tail/fan flex and supported rest use the same meshes. Full escape, actual swimming, feeding contact, sensory physiology, forces and measured gait timing are not implemented.
findings.evidenceScope: Authentic Roberto Pillon (Etrusko25) public-domain photograph compared with selected actual Naturalis diagnosis and FAO PDFpage12/printed239 whole profile, rostrum, P2 and antennular drawings. Naturalis and FAO give different tooth ranges; variable dentition is disclosed rather than treating one count as universal. No related Palaemon species gait data are fitted.
corrections: Replaced the repeated spherical draft abdomen with a continuous articulated tapered cuticle and pleural overlap cues.
Differentiated small anterior chelae from six main supporting limbs; added scaphocerites, serial swimmerets and five-part fan.
Replaced a milky material and adjusted overlap depth/opacity after actual rendered comparison; superseded captures retained privately.
Closed the flat frontal surface with a convex cuticle after close-up inspection; added partial mouthpart-palpal cues.
Reduced maximum local flex after detecting the fan crossing the support surface; rechecked final poses and reset.
findings.residual: Still partly stylized: transparency, pale overlap regions, fine chromatophore layout, ventral/mouthpart anatomy, fan setae/rays and detailed limb segmentation are incomplete. The selected rostrum and overall proportions are unmeasured. Close diagnostic views deliberately crop some distal antenna/tail portions; neutral views retain the whole organism. No independent taxonomic redetermination or biological validation.
